title: ZoomIt activates on AltGr+key instead of Ctrl+key

judgment.rationale: Multiple current-layout reports and the current aggregate RegisterHotKey implementation establish a reproducible modifier-identity defect.
evidence: French AZERTY and German QWERTZ reports reproduce through 0.101.2362.
AltGr is right Alt plus synthetic left Ctrl.
ZoomIt registers aggregate MOD_CONTROL/MOD_ALT hotkeys and cannot distinguish modifier sides.
judgment.recommended_action: Approve a physical-modifier matching design for ZoomIt.

fix_assessment.rationale: No existing fix distinguishes AltGr from intentional Ctrl/Ctrl+Alt ZoomIt shortcuts.

proposed_fixes.title: Match physical modifiers so AltGr is not Ctrl
proposed_fixes.root_cause: RegisterHotKey and the current shortcut representation collapse left/right modifier identity, allowing AltGr's synthetic Ctrl to activate ZoomIt shortcuts.
plan: Replace the affected global shortcut path with a physical-key matcher or shared low-level hook.
Preserve settings compatibility while matching left/right Ctrl and Alt and treating AltGr distinctly.
Add layout-specific regression coverage and ensure reload/unregister are atomic.
verification: French AZERTY AltGr+5 must type [ without recording.
German QWERTZ AltGr+8/9 must type brackets without mirror activation.
Intentional Ctrl+Alt shortcuts must still work and Ctrl alone must not trigger them.

confidence.rationale: The same mechanism is independently reported across layouts and is visible in current ZoomIt registration code.

issue_context.summary: ZoomIt activates configured Ctrl shortcuts when users type AltGr characters on non-US layouts.
known_information: Reports cover French AZERTY and German QWERTZ keyboards.
Current reports include ZoomIt recording and mirror actions on 0.101.2362.
A related existing fork mirror for Issue 50125 does not cover this issue.
inferences: Aggregate modifier matching treats AltGr as ordinary Ctrl or Ctrl+Alt.
Derived shortcut registration increases collisions for characters requiring AltGr.
issue_context.analysis: The issue is reproducible from keyboard layout semantics and current Win32 registration limitations; a physical modifier boundary is preferable to suppressing valid shortcuts.
initial_investigation: Inspected Zoomit.cpp registration, reload, WM_HOTKEY dispatch, settings interop, and existing zero-modifier derived-shortcut history.
Checked the discussion for current-layout confirmations and workarounds.

design.root_cause: ZoomIt uses aggregate modifier bits, so the synthetic left Ctrl emitted with right Alt for AltGr satisfies Ctrl-based registrations.
evidence: Current code uses RegisterHotKey with MOD_CONTROL/MOD_ALT.
The issue contains repeated AltGr collisions on French and German layouts.
Existing fixes only address zero-modifier derived shortcuts.

affected_files.purpose: Hotkey registration, dispatch, reload, and cleanup.

implementation_steps.current_behavior: Windows reports only aggregate modifier state.
implementation_steps.change: Match VK plus physical left/right modifier state in a fast low-level hook or equivalent shared path and post actions to the UI thread.
implementation_steps.code_block: if (rightAlt && leftCtrl) classify as AltGr; match configured physical modifiers; enqueue action.
edge_cases: Hook callback must do no I/O.
Avoid duplicate WM_HOTKEY and hook dispatch.
Unhook on shutdown and surface installation failure.
tests: Test AltGr, Ctrl+Alt, Ctrl-only, and reload/unregister behavior.

implementation_steps.current_behavior: Persisted shortcuts have no side-aware semantics.
implementation_steps.change: Keep old settings readable and define matching semantics without silently rewriting existing shortcuts.
implementation_steps.code_block: deserialize legacy shortcut; runtime matcher applies physical modifier policy.
edge_cases: Preserve existing configurations and US-layout behavior.
tests: Round-trip legacy and new shortcut representations.

verify: Build ZoomIt and native tests in x64 Debug.
Exercise French AZERTY and German QWERTZ E2E scenarios and confirm valid Ctrl+Alt shortcuts remain usable.
risks: Low-level hooks add lifecycle and latency concerns.
Changing AltGr semantics may affect users who intentionally configured it.
alternatives: Centralizing all shortcuts in Runner expands IPC scope.
Suppressing all Ctrl+Alt-derived shortcuts breaks valid configurations.

actions.label: Approve AltGr hotkey design
actions.note: Fork-side implementation only; no upstream action.

non_blocking_notes: Validate both layout-specific AltGr behavior and intentional Ctrl+Alt shortcuts.
